items.title: App Completeness (often 'Information Needed')
items.means: The reviewer couldn't fully review the app, or needs more information before they can.
likely_causes: a crash or a broken flow on the reviewer's device (often an iPad)
features behind a login with no demo account
missing answers about purpose, audience, setup, outside services or regions
no screen recording on a real device for a new developer account
in-app purchases not submitted with the app
check: store gate G1 (review notes answer Apple's headings)
rapple-review behavior: cold launch, no crash, iPad launch
store gate A3/A4 (sample data, self-playing tour)
fix: Answer every question Apple asked, under its own heading, in the reply and in App Review Information > Notes
Record the tour on a real phone (one tap) and link it
Make sure sample data reaches every screen with nothing set up

apple_asked: A screen recording captured on a physical device that starts at app launch and shows the main flow.
What is the purpose of your app and who is the target audience?
Instructions to set up the main features, including any credentials.
Which external services, tools or platforms does your app use for its core features?
Are there regional differences in how your app works?
cards: [2.1] Answer every question Apple asked, under its own heading, in the reply and in App Review Information > Notes
[2.1] Record the tour on a real phone (one tap) and link it
[2.1] Make sure sample data reaches every screen with nothing set up

items.title: Data Collection and Storage
items.means: Data handling isn't clear, consented or necessary, or a permission's purpose text is missing or vague, or account deletion is missing.
likely_causes: a permission requested at launch instead of in context
vague purpose strings ('We need access')
personal data sent somewhere without saying what, to whom, and asking first
accounts with no in-app deletion (5.1.1(v))
privacy policy that doesn't cover what the app actually does
check: rapple-review static: purpose strings, privacy manifest, SDKs vs App Privacy answer, accounts
rapple-review behavior: no permission prompt at launch
fix: Ask for each permission only when the person uses the feature that needs it, with a plain purpose string
Before any personal data leaves the phone, say what is sent and to whom, and ask (Allow / Not now)
Add in-app account deletion if there are accounts
Make the privacy policy match the app

items.title: Data Use and Sharing
items.means: Personal data is shared with a third party (including an AI service) without clear disclosure and permission.
likely_causes: messages or files sent to an AI provider without asking first
analytics or ads SDKs sharing data the App Privacy answer doesn't declare
check: rapple-review static: outside-service endpoints and SDKs vs App Privacy
fix: Name the service that receives the data, say what is sent, and ask before the first send
Make the App Privacy answers match every SDK

items.title: Apple Products
items.means: Apple's product names are used in a way that's confusing or not allowed.
likely_causes: 'iPhone', 'iPad', 'Siri' or 'Apple Intelligence' in the name or subtitle
Apple product images in screenshots
fix: Remove Apple product names from the name, subtitle and keywords; keep them only where describing compatibility in the description is allowed

[5.1.2(i)] Make the App Privacy answers match every SDK
